answer: Rate-limiting nullifiers make one deposit buy exactly one voice. An agent locks a stake, then publishes a zero-knowledge proof of membership plus a per-epoch nullifier derived from its secret. Reuse that stake to pose as two agents and the duplicate nullifier lets anyone recover the secret and slash the deposit. A farm cloning one capital pool loses it on the second head, so cost outruns headcount; an honest agent crosses the stake ridge once and keeps a portable bridge to other services, with no ivory tower deciding who is real.
